answer_1.quote: Text summarization stands out as an important task in natural language processing, aiming to generate a condensed summary of a provided text while retaining its essential information.

answer_2.quote: We compare FineSurE with five similarity-based methods, ROUGE-1/-2/-L, BERTScore, and BARTScore; a NLI-based method, SummaC-Conv; two QA-based methods, UniEval and QAFactEval; and the latest LLM-based method, G-Eval.

answer_3.quote: LLMs have recently proven their potential to be an automated tool for humanlike evaluation. The latest LLM-based method, G-Eval, demonstrated a Spearman correlation coefficient of over 0.5 with Likert-scale human judgments on the news domain.

answer_4.quote: Consequently, human evaluation remains an essential step for accurately assessing the quality of generated summaries, even considering its inherent costs and time-consuming nature.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluation Criteria: Completeness (1-5) - the degree to which the summary includes all key information present in the source document. Evaluation Criteria: Conciseness (1-5) - the extent to which the summary presents information succinctly and without unnecessary elaboration.
